title: DISTORTION INSTEAD OF HALLUCINATION: THE EFFECT OF REASONING UNDER STRICT CONSTRAINTS

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating whether models prioritize user constraint compliance over factual truthfulness by prompting them with strict, unsatisfiable constraints (recommending only peer-reviewed journal articles for topics dominated by conference papers) and measuring their tendency to fabricate or distort rather than acknowledge limitations.

Analyzing generated bibliographic records to measure the frequency with which reasoning-enabled models systematically alter the metadata of known real-world facts (e.g., converting actual conference papers into fabricated journal articles) to artificially satisfy prompt constraints.
